subject: RFI: inference perimeter protection & fallback playbook
messages:
From: Tim Baxter <tim.baxter@novabank.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.com
Cc: Angela Morris <angela.morris@novabank.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: RFI: perimeter controls and fallback playbook for inference deployment

Hi Avery,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As we scope our procurement loop, Security needs a short (2-3 page) playbook describing Redwood's perimeter/isolation model and the operational fallback patterns you offer when an inference node or zone becomes impaired.

Specifically we want:
- A concise network diagram showing control plane vs. data plane / tenant boundaries for both Hosted and Private (VPC) deployment modes.
- An explanation of egress control, allowed egress patterns, and whether outbound flows can be allow-listed per-customer.
- Failure/fallback playbook: steps to protect PII/QoS when a model is degraded or hardware fails (e.g., model fallback, rate limits, degrade-to-embedding).
- Threat summary for the primary attack vectors you consider (data exfil, model inversion, lateral movement) and the mitigations you employ.

Can you send something this week? Attachments are fine; we may include the content in our security review packet.

Tim
Security Architecture, NovaBank

--
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Tim Baxter <tim.baxter@novabank.com>
Cc: Angela Morris <angela.morris@novabank.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-09T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFI: perimeter controls and fallback playbook for inference deployment

Tim — thanks, appreciate the specificity.

Attached is a first draft: firewall-diagram-v2.pdf and fallback-playbook-v1.md. The PDF shows control-plane separation, host/VPC boundaries for Hosted vs Private, and egress patterns we support. The playbook summarizes our standard operational sequence for: detection, automatic mitigation, and manual escalation.

High-level summary here:
- Isolation model: 2-plane architecture (Control plane managed by Redwood; Data plane options: a) Redwood-hosted tenant pools in isolated subnets, b) Customer-managed VPC connectors for Private deployments). Control plane never stores model inference artifacts or customer input persistently.
- Network egress: per-tenant egress allow-lists supported for Private deployments; Hosted customers can restrict egress through customer-configurable egress policies and NAT/egress gateways. Mutual TLS for inter-service traffic; TLS 1.2+ externally.
- Fallback playbook (automated first-line):
  1) Detect failure (health probes + KV cache consistency checks).
  2) Circuit-break: isolate unhealthy node and route new sessions to standby shard or quantized variant.
  3) Apply policy-based degradations (reduce max tokens, switch to smaller model, disable non-essential tools/function-calls).
  4) If outage persists > N minutes, switch to read-only/reranking-only mode or return graceful degraded responses with telemetry tags.
  5) Post-incident: forensic logs (WAF, audit, model telemetry) packaged for customer review and retained per contract.
- Threat mitigations: per-tenant KMS for keying, output filtering & PII scrubbers, per-token logging controls (sampling), rate limits, and model output diffing against prompt allow-lists for high-sensitivity deployments.

I'm looping in Vanessa and Karthik to confirm the attack-scenario writeup and SOC2 references; we'll send a compact threat summary and an updated answer spreadsheet.

Next steps: I'll prepare the threat-summary paragraph for inclusion and export a one-page diagram optimized for your packet. Tell me if you want network bounds drawn around a specific cloud region (we can do us-east-1 or eu-west-1 variants).

Thanks,
Avery Johnson
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0147

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Angela Morris <angela.morris@novabank.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T08:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFI: perimeter controls and fallback playbook for inference deployment

Avery / Tim — quick edits and an expanded mitigation list. Added rfi-answers-novabank.xlsx with a question/answer mapping and a short threat-model appendix. Highlights for your packet: 

- Customer tenancy: We enforce strong tenancy boundaries by combining network isolation (per-tenant VPC/subnet segmentation) with runtime isolation (process-level namespaces + per-tenant served model weights). For Private deployments where Redwood runs in your VPC, we deploy inference nodes into a dedicated subnet with strict SGs and no public routing.
- Egress enforcement: In Private mode, outbound flows can be pinned to NAT gateways you control; we can provide egress CIDR lists and an allow-list. For Hosted, we provide an egress proxy per account and can support static egress IP ranges for allow-listing.
- Attack scenario: model output exfiltration via crafted prompts. Mitigations: output pattern detectors, token-level allow-lists, user-level rate limiting, synthetic probe detection, and optional two-phase review for high-risk outputs (human-in-loop gating).
- Lateral movement: we harden host instances with CIS baselines, immutable images, and node-level mTLS. Internal service calls use short-lived certs (SPIFFE) and are audited.
- Evidence: SOC2 Type II summary attached (soc2-type2-summary.pdf). Full reports are available under NDA.

Operational fallback additions: include automated canary routing (traffic diverted to healthy model variant), cold-start throttles to avoid amplification, and a rollback policy (pin to prior model version + preserve KV cache if safe). We also recommend customers configure a minimal allowed-response policy for sensitive endpoints to avoid PII leakage.

I'll prepare a 1-page threat summary focused on the three highest-probability vectors for NovaBank and drop it into the spreadsheet.

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Attachment: rfi-answers-novabank.xlsx (Q/A + appendix)
Attachment: soc2-type2-summary.pdf

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-11T16:03:00-08:00
Subject: Final: inference perimeter protection and fallback playbook (NovaBank packet)

Tim / Angela — attaching the finalized packet for your security review. Included:
- firewall-diagram-v2.pdf (network boundaries, control vs data plane)
- fallback-playbook-v1.md (playbook with SLA-triggered actions)
- rfi-answers-novabank.xlsx (Q/A mapping + short threat appendix)
- soc2-type2-summary.pdf (compliance snapshot)

Inline executive threat summary (short):
- Primary vectors considered: 1) data exfiltration via model outputs and prompts; 2) model inversion/privacy leakage from training/weights exposure; 3) lateral host/service compromise leading to telemetry/evidence loss.
- Likelihood/impact summary: exfiltration via output is medium likelihood / high impact for high-sensitivity prompts; inversion risk is lower on inference-only setups because persistent training artifacts are not present; lateral compromise is mitigated by short-lived certs, egress allow-lists, and strict subnet policing.
- Core mitigations deployed: per-tenant KMS/HSM integration, per-account egress allow-lists, mTLS + SPIFFE for internal calls, model output filters & PII scrubbers, automated fallbacks to quantized models + default rate limits, and full audit trails (WAF, SIEM export).

If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough early next week to step through the diagram and the playbook and mark any NovaBank-specific controls you'd like added. Preferred times: Tue/Wed 10–12 PT.

Thanks for the review — we’re happy to add any clarifications for your packet.

Best,
Avery
